title: Fan Fave: Mediterranean Haloumi Risotto
subtitle: with Zucchini and Red Pesto
description: We're not here to play faves – that's your job! By popular demand, we're repeating this fab 'fan-fave' recipe so you can love it (and eat it!) one more time. Keep telling us about the dishes you fell in love with by rating them in your account, so we can keep on bringing them back.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Finely chop the onion and tomato. Halve the zucchini lengthwise, then thinly slice. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Thinly slice the haloumi. Crumble the stock cubes into a heatproof jug, add 625ml (2½ cups) boiling water and stir to dissolve.

Start risotto: Heat 1 tbs olive oil in a medium deep frypan over medium heat. Cook the onion and garlic, stirring, for 3-4 mins until softened. Add the rice and tomato and cook, stirring, for 1-2 mins until the grains are well coated.

Simmer risotto: Add the stock to the rice mixture, reduce the heat to medium-low and cook, covered, for 10 mins. Stir in the zucchini and cook, covered, for a further 10 mins or until most of the liquid is absorbed and the rice is almost tender.

Pan-fry haloumi: Stir half the red pesto into the risotto and cook, uncovered, for 5 mins. Remove the pan from the heat and stand, covered, for 5 mins (see Kitchen 101). Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Meanwhile, heat 2 tsp olive oil in a medium frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the haloumi for 2 mins each side or until golden. Remove from the pan.
Serve up: Divide the risotto among bowls, top with the haloumi and spoon over the remaining red pesto. Enjoy!

Kitchen 101: Leaving the risotto to stand for a few minutes allows it to absorb the last of the liquid and then it's ready to serve up. Don't leave it sitting for longer than that or the rice will continue to soak up the liquid and may become stodgy. If this happens, simply add a little extra boiling water to loosen the risotto.
